claims.explanation: TW-37 is a BH3 mimetic that inhibits BCL2, BCL2L1 (BCL-XL), and MCL1, and its selectivity likely depends on the relative dependence of cancer cells on these anti-apoptotic proteins for survival. Lines with high expression of MCL1 or BCL2L1, or with mutations that activate survival signaling (e.g., KRAS, BRAF, PIK3CA, PTEN loss), may be more sensitive because they rely on these proteins to evade apoptosis. Conversely, high expression of BCL2 or BCL2L1 in some contexts could be protective if the drug's affinity is insufficient, but the observed sensitivity in pancreatic, gastric, and esophageal lines with KRAS/TP53 mutations suggests a role for oncogenic stress and MCL1 dependence.

features.basis: TW-37 binds MCL1 with high affinity (Ki 260 nM) and MCL1 overexpression is a known resistance factor to other BCL2 inhibitors; high MCL1 may predict sensitivity to TW-37.
TW-37 inhibits BCL-XL (Ki 1110 nM) and BCL-XL is a key anti-apoptotic protein in solid tumors; high expression may indicate dependence.
TW-37 was designed to target BCL2 (Ki 290 nM) and BCL2 overexpression is common in lymphomas and some solid tumors.
KRAS mutations are frequent in sensitive pancreatic and colorectal lines (SNU410, T3M4, CL11) and may drive MCL1 dependence.
BRAF mutations appear in sensitive melanoma lines (K029AX, IGR37) and may confer reliance on anti-apoptotic proteins.
PIK3CA mutations are present in several sensitive lines (KYSE510, HGC27, SNU840) and may activate survival signaling.
PTEN loss occurs in sensitive lines (FTC133, HEC265) and may increase dependence on BCL2 family proteins.
TP53 mutations are common in sensitive lines, but also in resistant lines, so this is weak evidence.
EGFR mutations are found in resistant lung lines (HCC4006, NCIH1650) and may indicate alternative survival pathways.
CDKN2A mutations appear in resistant lines (SNU1214, IPC298, MHHES1) but also in sensitive lines, so weak.
